newsitem.title: ROMANIA: IMF's Camdessus seeks quick Romania reforms.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus seeks quick Romania reforms.

text.p: International Monetary Fund head Michel Camdessus urged Romania on Saturday to cut budget expenditure and restructure its economy to win the Fund's approval for restoring suspending credits.

Camdessus told a news conference after a day of talks with the new centrist leaders he was confident a new loan accord could be concluded after talks get under way next month, but only if ministers acted quickly.

"Structural change, privatisation, freeing of prices, reduction and progresive cancellation of many subsidies which are a way of mis-allocating scarce resources. All of that must be done and must be done soon," Camdessus said.

The Fund suspended a $460 million accord this year after criticising the previous leftist cabinet's foreign exchange market restrictions and overspending ahead of last month's election which brought President Emil Constantinescu to power.
A week-long mission by Fund experts immediately after the election revealed grim economic indicators, with inflation, budget and current account deficits far beyond targets.

Camdessus, the IMF's Managing Director, said programmes under the former government broke down because it failed to reduce soft credits, maintain free exchange markets or restructure energy-intensive sectors.

"If you want this programme to succeed you will have to address these structural problems," he said. "The government knows this pretty well that this action in stabilisation and structural changes must be performed rapidly."
A government statement issued after talks with Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said authorities would get the IMF's backing if it implemented key measures within four months.
It said these included controls on budget spending, gradual adjustment of prices to world levels and reductions in monthly inflation to 2.5 percent from its current level of 5.8 percent.
But Camdessus said no deadline had been discussed.
"I told the government: Get your programme ready," he said. "When it's ready, give us a call and we'll tell you what we think of it. If it's good and credible, we will finance it."
He said high inflation, a budget deficit of between 5.5 to 6 percent of gross domestic product and a current account deficit of 5 percent of gdp compounded the government's task.
Camdessus earlier repeated the IMF's contention that ministers had inherited a situation worse than earlier thought.
He praised the government's initial programme, approved by parliament last week, as "courageous" and said the Fund would do what it could to rally international support for it.
That programme contains few figures but calls broadly for restraint in budget spending, liberalisation of foreign exchange markets and increased benefits.
As Camdessus arrived on Friday, Ciorbea announced increases in fuel prices in line with IMF recommendations.
